state: JevCode pipeline gate tuning, round 10. The automated pipeline (scripts/pipeline.mjs) is built and working end-to-end: fetch GitHub ecosystem data, Jev gate-1 (worth publishing? where?), commit, build, astro check, full internal link check, Jev gate-2 (release ready? risk?), push, atomic deploy, jsonl audit log. Design came from round 9: scheduler vps_cron 0.41 (weak, hybrid was 0.30), stages stars_plus_detect 0.74, two_stage Jev gates 0.95, auto_deploy_safety 0.49 (undecided), frequency daily 0.88, landing branch_pr 0.63. PROBLEM DISCOVERED IN TESTING: gate-1 currently judges raw star-count deltas and returns worth=0.08-0.18 (HOLD) for small changes (e.g. 4 repos changed by 1-5 stars overnight after a big refresh was already applied manually today: 603/318/324/4026 stars already live from this session's manual run). So the gate is behaving correctly-ish (small deltas are indeed not release-worthy), but this creates a question about batching: should the pipeline batch small changes until a threshold, instead of rejecting them? Also the fresh fetch just found 4 repos moved 1-5 stars beyond what was manually committed — trivial. Current deployed ecosystem data is from today's manual refresh (already the largest jump: e.g. one repo 1979 -> 4026). Questions: how should gate-1 handle batching of small deltas? What threshold logic? Should auto-deploy be enabled for gate-approved releases (round 9 was 0.49, still undecided)? Where should cron actually run (vps vs local vs github actions — round 9 gave vps_cron only 0.41 over hybrid 0.30)?

batching_policy.instructions: How should gate-1 handle small star-count deltas that individually fail the worth-publishing threshold?

criteria.batch_by_magnitude: Accumulate deltas in a pending state; release when cumulative change magnitude crosses a threshold (e.g. any repo +10% or total +50 stars since last release)
criteria.batch_by_age: Accumulate and release whatever exists at the weekly boundary (max staleness 7 days), regardless of magnitude
criteria.both: Release when EITHER magnitude threshold OR 7-day staleness is crossed, whichever first
criteria.never_batch: Never batch; each daily cycle publishes only if that day's delta alone is significant

magnitude_threshold.instructions: If magnitude-based: what minimum per-repo relative change justifies an immediate release?

auto_deploy_final.instructions: Final call now that gates are implemented and tested: should gate-approved releases auto-deploy to production without human click? (round 9 was 0.49)

criteria.true: Yes: data-only updates with build+check+link+two-Jev-gate protection may auto-deploy
criteria.false: No: keep human approval for production

scheduler_final.instructions: Where should the cron actually run? (round 9: vps_cron 0.41, hybrid 0.30 — weak signal)

criteria.vps_cron: VPS cron: always-on, repo cloned there, API key on server, local symlink deploy
criteria.local_cron: Operator's mac: has everything already; misses runs when asleep
criteria.github_actions_pr: GitHub Actions: fetch+gates+commit+PR; deploy stays manual/vps pull
criteria.github_actions_full: GitHub Actions with SSH secret for full auto-deploy

stale_data_display.instructions: How should the site display star data freshness given a batching policy?

criteria.date_stamp: Show 'data as of <date>' on the ecosystem page, auto-updated per release
criteria.no_stamp: No stamp; numbers are understood to be approximate
criteria.live_widget: Client-side live fetch of stars on page load (rate-limit and privacy concerns)

gate1_instructions_tuning.instructions: Should gate-1's worth-publishing question be rewritten to explicitly reference the batching policy (so it judges 'should this batch release now' rather than 'is this delta significant')?

criteria.true: Yes: gate should evaluate the batch + staleness together
criteria.false: No: keep gate as pure significance judge; batching logic in code
